title: Pilot study on platelet–leukocyte aggregates (PLAs) in aortic valve disease and following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI)
summary:
Aortic valve diseases, in particular aortic valve stenosis, are common in older adults and can lead to shortness of breath, reduced physical capacity, and heart failure. A common treatment in older patients is the replacement of the diseased valve with an artificial valve that is implanted using a heart catheter. In some patients, blood clots can form on the artificial valve after this procedure, but the reasons for this are not yet fully understood.

The aim of this study is to investigate whether certain changes in the blood, in which blood platelets bind to white blood cells, are related to the development of these blood clots. Blood samples from patients will be analyzed before and after valve implantation and compared with samples from individuals who already have known clots on an artificial heart valve, as well as with samples from individuals without aortic valve disease.

Blood samples are taken only during routine blood tests that are part of standard medical care, without additional needle punctures or procedures. This study is designed to provide initial insights and to support the planning of future larger studies.
conditions: Other specified complications of cardiac and vascular prosthetic devices, implants and grafts

interventions.name:
Arm 1:
Patients with clinically relevant aortic valve disease undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), in whom platelet–leukocyte aggregates (PLAs) are assessed at predefined time points using routine blood samples obtained before and after the procedure.
Patients with previously diagnosed prosthetic valve thrombosis after TAVI, in whom PLAs are assessed twice using routine blood samples.
Control participants with a comparable cardiovascular risk profile but without relevant valvular heart disease, in whom PLAs are assessed once using routine blood samples.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
written consent
clear assignment to one of the three study groups
Exclusion criteria:
Acute systemic infection
Inability to provide informed consent
